title: Bamako cattle-market vendors' work stoppage against closures and relocation
location: Cattle markets in Bamako, including Niamana; other participant locations unspecified
organizer: Collective of Bamako cattle-market vendors; formal organizer not identified

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The article reports vendors stopping work across Bamako markets but no public assembly or number present at one time; 50-person gathering threshold is not established.

start_date.summary: The Oct25 article says the work stoppage began Tuesday; calendar mapping yields Oct22. This is a weekday-to-date derivation, not a printed numeric date.

location.summary: The vendors' stoppage concerned cattle markets in Bamako; Niamana and two previously closed sites are named but precise gathering locations are unknown.

demands.summary: Text describes opposition to the government's market-closure/relocation decision and a demand to release the Niamana market chair and hear vendors' demands. The ministry reports that, at a separate September 20 policy meeting, sector actors had asked for a moratorium on relocation; that earlier meeting is contextual and is not coded as the October start.

participants.summary: No public gathering or simultaneous turnout is described; threshold unresolved.

organizer.summary: Collective of Bamako cattle-market vendors; no named organizer.

state_response.summary: Article alleges an Oct23 abduction by State Security based on an unnamed security source, reportedly connected to the strike; no coded response variable is conclusively established.

source_origin.summary: Article credits RFI; no independent source relationship is claimed.

state_target.summary: The ministry identifies the district governor/transition government as the decision-maker on market closure; Le Radar says vendors' strike continued until the transition government heard their demands.

notes: This is a candidate for review, not an inclusion. The underlying closure of cattle markets began 19 September under a government decision; October work stoppage began Oct22. A later release/continuity date is not established. Le Radar explicitly credits RFI, so it is not independent corroboration. Bamada body was tool-inaccessible; Maliweb open returned unrelated homepage content. The Ministry's Oct8-posted report describes a Sep20 meeting and prior request for a moratorium; that date is outside this unit and is context only.
open_questions: Did vendors or consumers hold a public march, assembly, picket, or other gathering while the stoppage was underway?
If so, when and where did the qualifying gathering begin, and how many were present simultaneously?
Can a separate contemporary source confirm the event, state demand, and any public gathering independently of RFI?
What were the organizer and formal demands in the union/market leaders' records?
When did the stoppage and any gathering end; was the market chair released or were the markets relocated?
